name: Firebolt
tagline: Low-latency analytical database with a Postgres-compliant dialect, as cloud service or self-hosted Core.
description: Firebolt is an analytical database focused on low-latency, high-concurrency SQL for data-intensive applications. Its engine combines sparse primary indexes, aggregating indexes and a distributed vectorized executor over decoupled object storage, and its SQL dialect follows PostgreSQL. Beyond the managed cloud on AWS, Firebolt Core is a free, self-hosted edition that runs from a single binary to Kubernetes clusters and reads Iceberg. Firebolt says a fully open-source release is in preview. It targets customer-facing analytics and AI-agent workloads; the ecosystem is smaller than the big warehouses'.

license.name: Elastic License 2.0 (Firebolt Core); open-source release in preview

pricing.notes: Firebolt Core is free to self-host without usage limits; the managed service bills per engine node-hour plus storage.

scale.notes: Engines scale out by nodes and clusters; storage on S3. Core scales from one node to many on Kubernetes.

strengths: Sparse and aggregating indexes give low-latency queries at high concurrency
PostgreSQL-compliant SQL dialect eases tooling and migration
Free self-hosted Core edition with no usage limits
Decoupled storage and compute with workload-isolated engines
Reads Iceberg tables for lakehouse use
weaknesses: Smaller community and integration ecosystem than Snowflake or ClickHouse
Core's license is source-available (ELv2), not OSI open source, until the OSS release ships
Managed service runs only on AWS
Index design still matters for best latency
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a mature, broad SaaS ecosystem
